Violence in relationships cannot be condoned, and it is not a private matter.
Violence could affect anyone, from children to the elderly.
Unexplained wounds and bruises on the arms/body could be a sign of violence in relationship.
Significant changes in mood e.g. depression, trauma and anxiety could be a symptom of violence in a relationship
Signs of constant hunger, dehydration, malnourishment, poor personal hygiene and untreated medical conditions could be symptoms of violence in a relationship.
A sign of violence in relationship could be sudden intense fear and avoidance of a particular person, place or object.
Everyone has a responsibility to help their family, friends and loved ones who are experiencing violence in their lives.
The reporting of abuse does not worsen after your intervention and does not break up families. It can save lives and families.
You can call the National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline at 1800 777 0000.
You can call the police at 999 or SMS 70999 for emergencies.
